title: ARWP Site Readiness Gate
purpose: Decide whether a site has enough technical, content, identity, publication and measurement integrity to begin or interpret a Search/AI acquisition experiment without reducing readiness to a vanity score.

checks.requirement: The site states the primary user/problem/task it serves.
The site or adoption record states what the site intentionally does not cover.
A bounded priority page cohort exists for measurement instead of treating every URL equally.
At least one site-specific downstream task or conversion is defined.
Priority URLs return the intended successful HTTP status.
Search/answer crawler access is intentional and not accidentally blocked.
Indexability, canonical target and sitemap membership agree for priority pages.
Sitemap freshness represents significant content changes rather than unconditional build time.
Redirects, locale variants, filters and query variants do not create competing canonical identities.

Search identity scope is classified at hostname level. A project under owner.github.io/project/ does not pretend to own a separate Google site-name/Search-favicon scope; distinct brands use an independent hostname when that identity matters.
The first useful content states the page's answer or concrete value.
Priority pages add original evidence, data, experience, analysis, calculation, curation or an executable utility.
Material factual claims have inspectable evidence or an explicit uncertainty/evidence boundary.
Important sections can be linked and retrieved directly.
A direct landing visitor can perform a useful task without first understanding the site's internal taxonomy.
Canonical entities use stable reusable identities across public representations.
Structured data and machine-readable exports do not contradict visible public facts.
Dataset metadata describes a real reusable corpus when dataset surfaces are used.
Published entity relationships are semantically meaningful rather than generated keyword adjacency.
Search/answer retrieval policy is reviewed separately from model-training policy where provider controls differ.
llms.txt/skills/API/MCP/A2A/WebMCP/ARD/ARWP declarations correspond to real useful content or capability.
Runtime capabilities are backed by runtime evidence rather than static metadata only.
Primary tasks expose semantic HTML, usable links/buttons and meaningful accessible names before agent-specific optimization.
Baseline start/end and change timestamp are recorded.
Google generative AI evidence comes from the dedicated provider report; ordinary Search impressions are not relabeled.
Bing citation/cited-page/grounding-query evidence is retained when available.
AI referrals retain source/referrer/UTM evidence when available.
AI crawler requests, response success and policy state are retained when edge/server evidence is available.
A first-party task outcome is measured for referred visits where the product supports it.
Derived ratios use the same provider/population/window unless an explicit join key exists.
No cross-provider pseudo-conversion rate such as Bing citations divided by Google AI impressions is used.
No synthetic AI visibility score is treated as the system of record.
Missing metrics remain missing/partial/unavailable rather than becoming zero.
Provider exports/evidence locations are preserved for replay and review.
Hypothesis IDs and tested implementation actions are recorded before outcome review.
Treatment pages form a bounded cohort; large generated sites start with priority cohorts before scale.
Comparable unchanged pages are retained when practical; otherwise a dated pre-change baseline is preserved.
Success signals, guardrails and stop conditions are defined before measurement.
Indexable entity pages pass the ARWP Index Worthiness demand, unique-value, standalone-utility, provenance, connectivity, canonical-identity, freshness and entity-depth review.
The Search-facing sitemap is a curated canonical cohort of index-candidate pages, not a dump of every route emitted by the build.
Generated pages, query/filter variants and template families are reviewed for independent value; generic filler text is not used to justify Search publication.
Priority deep pages have useful crawlable paths from collections/hubs or related entities.
Deep-page contribution is measured separately for exposure, citations, referrals and task outcomes.
Crawl/index growth is reviewed against useful discovery growth; raw page count is not a success metric.
